???+ remember "Before you start, remember"

    ??? question "Which MLIR type names a shaped, typed reference to a region of memory, with a layout such as row-major order?"

        A memref. It behaves like a Vortex `&mut` argument, except that nothing in the type itself rules out two memrefs aliasing.

        Introduced in [M2. Reading MLIR](m2-reading-mlir.md).

    ??? question "What is MLIR's single unit of meaning, used for everything from one addition to a whole function?"

        An operation. Every operation, whatever its dialect, is built from the same fixed set of parts, results, operands, regions, attributes, a type and a location.

        Introduced in [M2. Reading MLIR](m2-reading-mlir.md).

    ??? question "What do we call an ordered list of blocks that belongs to an operation, whose meaning that operation itself decides?"

        A region. A function's body and a loop's body are each one region.

        Introduced in [M2. Reading MLIR](m2-reading-mlir.md).

    ??? question "Which v0.1 type holds a fixed number of values of one type, with sizes known at compile time, such as `[f32; 4]`?"

        A fixed-size array. Its element type and every dimension are part of its type.

        Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#71-array-types).
